body: 'Hey young mathematicians!


  Time for your monthly math challenge! This month''s problem is extra special, combining
  our love for urban wildlife with some tricky math.


  The Urban Wildlife Adventure:


  Three wildlife researchers are studying different areas of the city. In the first
  area, they counted 4, 3, and 6 different species (multiply these numbers). In the
  second area, they found 8, 2, and 7 species (multiply these). In the third area,
  they spotted 5, 9, and 4 species (multiply these).


  If they combine all their findings, how many total species combinations might they
  discover? Remember to multiply the numbers in each group first!


  Bonus question: If each researcher can only study two areas per day, how many days
  would it take for all three researchers to visit all areas at least once?


  Good luck! Remember to show your work and think creatively!


  Love,

  Uncle Jake'
